passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Ameren, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, is a public utility holding company whose primary assets are its equity interests in its subsidiaries. Ameren’s subsidiaries are separate, independent legal entities with separate businesses, assets, and liabilities. Dividends on Ameren’s common stock and the payment of expenses by Ameren depend on distributions made to it by its subsidiaries. Below is a summary description of Ameren’s principal subsidiaries – Ameren Missouri, Ameren Illinois, and ATXI. Ameren also has other subsidiaries that conduct other activities, such as providing shared services. A more detailed description can be found in Note 1 – Summary of Significant Accounting Policies under Part II, Item 8, of this report. • Ameren Missouri operates a rate-regulated electric generation, transmission, and distribution business and a rate-regulated natural gas distribution business in Missouri. • Ameren Illinois operates rate-regulated electric transmission, electric distribution, and natural gas distribution businesses in Illinois. • ATXI operates a FERC rate-regulated electric transmission business in the MISO. Ameren has four segments: Ameren Missouri, Ameren Illinois Electric Distribution, Ameren Illinois Natural Gas, and Ameren Transmission. The Ameren Missouri segment includes all of the operations of Ameren Missouri. Ameren Illinois Electric Distribution consists of the electric distribution business of Ameren Illinois. Ameren Illinois Natural Gas consists of the natural gas business of Ameren Illinois. Ameren Transmission primarily consists of the aggregated electric transmission businesses of Ameren Illinois and ATXI. See Note 16 – Segment Information under Part II, Item 8, of this report for further discussion of Ameren’s and Ameren Illinois’ segments. Ameren’s and Ameren Missouri’s financial statements are prepared on a consolidated basis and therefore include the accounts of their majority-owned subsidiaries. All intercompany transactions have been eliminated. Ameren Illinois has no subsidiaries. All tabular dollar amounts are in millions, unless otherwise indicated. The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the financial statements contained in this Form 10-K. We intend for this discussion to provide the reader with information that will assist in understanding our financial statements, the changes in certain key items in those financial statements, and the primary factors that accounted for those changes, as well as how certain accounting principles affect our financial statements. The discussion also provides information about the financial results of our business segments to provide a better understanding of how those segments and their results affect the financial condition and results of operations of Ameren as a whole. Discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2023, including comparisons with the year ended December 31, 2024, is included in Item 7 of our Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Investors should review carefully the following material risk factors and the other information contained in this report. The risks that the Ameren Companies face are not limited to those in this section. There may be further risks and uncertainties that are not presently known or that are not currently believed to be material that may adversely affect the results of operations, financial position, and liquidity of the Ameren Companies. REGULATORY AND LEGISLATIVE RISKS We are subject to extensive regulation of our businesses. We are subject to federal, state, and local regulation. The extensive regulatory frameworks, some of which are more specifically identified in the following risk factors, regulate, among other matters, the electric and natural gas utility industries; the rate and cost structure of utilities, including an allowed ROE; the operation of nuclear power plants; the construction and operation of generation, transmission, and distribution facilities; the acquisition, disposal, depreciation and amortization of assets and facilities; the electric transmission system reliability; and wholesale and retail competition. In the planning and management of our operations, we must address the effects of existing and proposed laws and regulations and potential changes in our regulatory frameworks, including new interpretations of existing regulations, as well as executive orders, initiatives by federal and state legislatures, RTOs, utility regulators, and taxing authorities, and actions by local jurisdictions that may affect the constructing or siting of facilities. Significant changes in the nature of the regulation of our businesses, including expiration or discontinuation of, or significant changes to, existing regulatory mechanisms, and the presidential administration’s approach to environmental and energy policy and resultant changes in regulatory enforcement priorities, and/or evolving interpretations of existing regulatory requirements, could require changes to our business planning, strategy and management of our businesses and could adversely affect our results of operations, financial position, and liquidity. Failure to obtain adequate rates or regulatory approvals in a timely manner; failure to obtain necessary licenses or permits from regulatory authorities; the impact of new or modified laws, regulations, standards, interpretations, or other legal requirements; or increased compliance costs could adversely affect our results of operations, financial position, and liquidity. The electric and natural gas rates that we are allowed to charge are determined through regulatory proceedings, which are subject to intervention and appeal. Rates are also subject to legislative actions, which are largely outside of our control. Certain events could prevent us from recovering our costs in a timely manner or at all, or from earning adequate returns on our investments. The rates that we are allowed to charge for our utility services significantly influence our results of operations, financial position, and liquidity. credit_strengths.text: Ameren's regulated utility footprint across Missouri, Illinois and MISO transmission delivers stable, rate-recoverable cash flows. Operating cash flow has grown steadily over the past three fiscal years, and operating margin sits near the sector median, reflecting constructive rate outcomes and cost recovery. This scale and regulatory diversity underpin the issuer's capacity to fund ongoing capital programs.

Interest coverage is modestly above the sector median, and operating income has expanded materially in the latest fiscal year. The utility's regulated earnings base supports predictable debt service, while the long-dated maturity profile, with the bulk of obligations due beyond five years, limits near-term refinancing pressure and provides flexibility to manage capital spending.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight extensive federal, state and local regulation, including allowed ROE, rate case intervention and appeal, and potential adverse changes in regulatory frameworks. Failure to obtain adequate rates or timely approvals could impair cost recovery and liquidity. This regulatory concentration is a core credit risk for Ameren's multi-jurisdictional utility operations.

Debt maturities show a steady annual refinancing need, with a notable bullet due in the fourth year, while short-term borrowings remain outstanding. The debt note confirms the holding company structure relies on subsidiary distributions to service parent obligations. Refinancing risk is manageable given the long-dated profile, but dependence on capital markets remains a structural feature.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow is negative as capital expenditure exceeds operating cash flow, a common profile for rate-base growth utilities. The cash flow-to-debt ratio is above the sector median, but the indicative financial risk profile remains highly leveraged. Debt service depends on continued access to capital markets and timely regulatory recovery of invested capital.

Liquidity is tight, with current liabilities exceeding current assets and a current ratio well below the sector median. Cash balances are minimal relative to debt, and the company relies on short-term borrowings and revolving facilities. This working capital position, combined with negative free cash flow, constrains financial flexibility and heightens dependence on external funding.

overall_credit_view.text: Ameren's credit profile reflects a large regulated utility with stable cash generation but elevated leverage. Gross and net leverage are marginally above the sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is highly leveraged. Interest coverage is adequate, though free cash flow is negative. The utility's scale and regulatory diversity support the credit, but the balance sheet leaves limited headroom.

Our forward view is that leverage will remain elevated while the capital program continues and shareholder dividends absorb a significant portion of operating cash flow. The company's ability to manage regulatory outcomes and refinance maturities will be critical. We see the credit as stable but sensitive to adverse rate decisions or funding cost increases.

credit_strengths.text: Ameren於密蘇里州、伊利諾州及MISO輸電網絡的受規管公用事業版圖，帶來穩定且可透過費率收回的現金流。過去三個財政年度，營運現金流穩步增長，而營運利潤率接近行業中位數，反映有利的費率結果及成本回收。此規模及監管多元性，支撐發行人為持續資本計劃提供資金的能力。
利息覆蓋率略高於行業中位數，而最近一個財政年度的營運收入大幅擴張。該公用事業的受規管盈利基礎支持可預測的債務償付，而長年期到期結構（大部分債務於五年後到期）限制了近期再融資壓力，並提供管理資本開支的靈活性。

key_risks.text: 風險因素凸顯廣泛的聯邦、州及地方監管，包括允許的ROE、費率案件介入及上訴，以及監管框架潛在的不利變化。未能取得足夠費率或及時批准，可能損害成本回收及流動性。此監管集中度是Ameren跨司法管轄區公用事業營運的核心信用風險。
債務到期顯示穩定的年度再融資需求，其中第四年有一筆顯著的子彈式到期，而短期借款仍未償還。債務附註確認控股公司結構依賴附屬公司分派以償付母公司債務。鑑於長年期結構，再融資風險可控，但依賴資本市場仍屬結構性特徵。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流為負，因資本開支超過營運現金流，此乃費率基礎增長型公用事業的常見情況。現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，但指示性財務風險狀況仍為高度槓桿。債務償付取決於能否持續進入資本市場及已投資本的及時監管回收。
流動性緊張，流動負債超過流動資產，而流動比率遠低於行業中位數。現金結餘相對債務極少，公司依賴短期借款及循環信貸。此營運資金狀況，加上負自由現金流，限制了財務靈活性並加劇對外部資金的依賴。

overall_credit_view.text: Ameren的信用狀況反映一家大型受規管公用事業，現金產生穩定但槓桿偏高。總槓桿及淨槓桿略高於行業中位數，而指示性財務風險狀況為高度槓桿。利息覆蓋率足夠，儘管自由現金流為負。該公用事業的規模及監管多元性支持信用，但資產負債表留下的緩衝有限。
我們的前瞻觀點是，當資本計劃持續而股東股息吸收營運現金流的顯著部分時，槓桿將維持偏高。公司管理監管結果及為到期債務再融資的能力將至關重要。我們認為信用穩定，但對不利費率決定或融資成本上升敏感。
